name: The Intertwining of Binding and Unbinding in the Religions of the Book.
headline: The Intertwining of Binding and Unbinding in the Religions of the Book.
copyrightNotice: Copyright held by the author(s). Published in the Journal for Cultural and Religious Theory.
abstract: The religions of the book, Islam, Christianity, and Judaism, all accept the Mosaic Pentateuch. They thus share the belief, expressed in Genesis, in a God who fashioned the world. From this belief they draw two very different lessons. The first is a universal claim drawn from the conception of a unique creator of the universe.
